transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I can’t shake this feeling that people at work are watching what I buy and messing with the launch numbers. Like even some of the vendors feel involved. My supervisor has shown me reports that don’t really prove it, but it still feels like they’re trying to make me look stupid.
Even when your supervisor shows you reports that don’t support it, are you still certain that people at work are watching what you buy and altering the launch numbers?

Yeah… I mean, I know the reports don’t show it, but I still feel pretty sure something’s going on. It’s like people at work, and even some vendors, are tracking what I buy and changing the launch numbers so I look bad. I can’t really shake it.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Yeah… sometimes. Like when I’m in the stockroom, or driving back from a vendor meeting, I’ll hear a man’s voice like it’s right behind me. It’ll say, “Move faster, Scott,” or laugh at what I picked. But when I turn around, nobody’s there.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah. There have been a lot of weeks where I’ll only sleep like three or four hours, but I wake up feeling wired, like I’m ready to go. I don’t even feel tired. It feels like lying in bed is just wasting time when I could be getting things done.
During those times when you only slept a few hours and still felt wired, did you also feel unusually euphoric or unusually irritable?

Yeah, both, I guess. At first I can feel really up, like everything’s opening up and I can do anything. But then if someone at work questions one of my purchase orders or tells me to slow down, I’ll snap at them way harder than I mean to.
Have you heard that voice during times when your mood felt normal, not especially up or irritable?

Yeah. It wasn’t only when I was all wired or irritated. There was a calmer stretch where I was sleeping more normal, and I still heard the voice in the stockroom. I also felt like people were tracking what I was buying for a few weeks, even though my mood didn’t feel that extreme then.
Have there been times when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had days where I felt down, but I don’t know if it was most of the day nearly every day for two weeks. I haven’t really kept track like that.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or felt people were tracking you while your mood was otherwise normal?

Yeah, I think so. There was a calmer stretch where I was sleeping more normally, not feeling all sped up or like I was running everything, and I still had a few weeks where I thought people were tracking what I was buying. I was also still hearing the voice in the stockroom during that time.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurologic condition that started before these experiences began?
Not that I know of. I haven’t been diagnosed with anything medical or neurologic before this started.
Have the voice and the feeling that people were tracking you lasted for at least one month in total?
Yes. It’s been way longer than a month. The voice and that feeling like people were tracking me have been going on for, I’d say, about ten months now.
Since these experiences began, has your ability to do your job or take care of yourself gotten noticeably worse?

Yes, definitely. My job has gotten worse. I’ve missed buying deadlines, messed up some vendor relationships, and made some impulsive purchasing decisions that got me formally warned by my supervisor.

And outside work, I’ve pulled back a lot. I don’t really see friends like I used to, and I stopped going to gallery nights and volleyball weekends, which used to be normal for me.
Have you had a period of at least one week when you felt unusually energized or irritable most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes. I get stretches like that where I feel really keyed up, like everything in the city is kind of opening up for me. And then if someone questions me at work, like about a purchase order or tells me I need to slow down, I snap way harder than I mean to.
Since these problems began, has feeling unusually energized or irritable been present for most of the time overall?

Yeah, I think so. Looking back, most of the time since this started I’ve been in those wired or irritable stretches — working too much, feeling overly sure of myself, and getting hard to slow down. There have been calmer times, but they’re shorter in between.
During a time when you were not feeling especially up, irritable, or depressed, did the voice and the feeling that people were tracking you continue for at least two weeks?

Yes. There was a calmer stretch where I was sleeping more normally and didn’t feel so… revved up, like I was running everything. But even then, for a few weeks, I still thought people were tracking my buys, and I still heard the voice in the stockroom.
Has there ever been a time when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had bad days where I felt down or worn out, but I don’t know if it was most of the day every day for two whole weeks. I haven’t kept track like that.
When the voice and the feeling that people were tracking you were happening, were you also feeling unusually up or irritable at the same time?

Yes. During those weeks when I was barely sleeping and talking nonstop about sneaker trends, I felt really charged up, like I couldn’t be touched at work. And at the same time I was convinced vendors were messing with the numbers, and I’d hear that voice telling me to move faster.
When you heard the voice, did it ever tell you that you had special powers or an important mission?
Not really special powers or a mission, no. It’s more like a man’s voice behind me saying stuff like, “Move faster, Scott,” or laughing at what I picked. I’ll turn around and nobody’s there.
Before any of this started, was there ever a manic period when you felt unusually energized or irritable but were not hearing the voice?

Yeah, I think so. I get these stretches where I feel like everything’s kind of opening up for me, like the whole city is there for me. And then if someone questions a purchase order or tells me to slow down, I snap at them way harder than I mean to.
Since these problems began, have you had at least two straight weeks when you were hearing the voice or felt tracked while not feeling unusually up, irritable, or depressed?

Yeah. There was a calmer stretch where I was sleeping more normal, and I didn’t feel all hyped up or like I was running everything. But for a few weeks I still thought people were tracking what I was buying, and I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom.
Has there ever been a time when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks while you were also hearing the voice or feeling that people were tracking you?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I had a solid two weeks like that where I was depressed most of the day every day. I’ve had bad days, but I can’t say it was that steady while the voice or tracking stuff was happening.

patient.answer: Yeah. There was a calmer stretch where I was sleeping more normal, and I didn’t feel all hyped up or like I was running everything. But for a few weeks I still thought people were tracking what I was buying, and I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms have also occurred during a major depressive episode, which would support schizoaffective disorder over bipolar I disorder with psychotic features or schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Has there ever been a time when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks while you were also hearing the voice or feeling that people were tracking you?

target_item.reason: The question asks about a depressive episode lasting at least two weeks occurring while psychotic symptoms were present, but the provided symptom profile does not include depressive mood or major depressive episode symptoms.

patient.answer: I’m not really sure. I don’t think I had a solid two weeks like that where I was depressed most of the day every day. I’ve had bad days, but I can’t say it was that steady while the voice or tracking stuff was happening.

inference.note: Psychosis has persisted for at least 2 weeks outside any mood episode, there is a clear manic syndrome present for much of the illness, and there is no evidence of sustained major depressive episodes. This rules out F31.2 and F20.0, leaving schizoaffective disorder, manic type.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) for about 10 months, clear manic episodes with decreased need for sleep, elevated/irritable mood, increased energy, grandiosity/overconfidence, and impairment. Critically, psychotic symptoms also persisted for at least 2 weeks during a euthymic/non-depressed, non-manic period, supporting schizoaffective disorder rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic symptoms. Depressive episodes were not clearly established, fitting the manic type.
